description: One report of everything that stands between a Game Kit project (gkp_…) and a FINISHED game of its genre — run it before telling the user a game is done, and again after each round of fixes. It aggregates, by severity (blocker / major / minor): creatures (slots drawn as a capsule, models without a skeleton, missing movement or action clips, the animation chain in progress), controls (no control scheme, the suggested one, keys shared by two actions in one mode, playable actions without a key), content (missing capabilities, required slots, the game.engine report), the last headless playtest (failures, warnings, the keys / models / animations probes, the checks of what the game chose — promised gestures, fullscreen, right button, pointer capture, texts —, capabilities no probe covers), the frame rate measured in a real page (sections.framerate: measured, or unverified — never call the game smooth while it is unverified; under 30 fps it is a major defect), keys shown in game (completeness common.no_key_hints, major: a ui.prompts help bar, build.placement keyHints or ui.menu keyHints turned on, a HUD text that lists keys or mouse buttons — no key on screen outside a tutorial), the default screens (sections.screens: on the KitHost page the host mounts them; a compiled module or a custom page must mount the menu, Options › Controls and Video, fullscreen when offered and the prompts from the bindings through the kits’ web views or adapter — a missing kit or a failing screen is a major defect, and a screen no real page has opened is screens.unverified, a major defect: say "not verified", never done) and completeness: what a finished game of the genre has beyond the literal request (MOBA: distinct heroes with Q/W/E/R, minions, towers, jungle monsters, shop, respawn; FPS: weapon, ammo, reload, crosshair, enemies; platformer: checkpoints, collectibles, end of level; racing: laps, ranking, AI opponents… and for every game a way to win AND to lose, title / pause / end screens, sound, a HUD, touch controls), checked against facts of the project, never a declaration. Each defect carries fix { tool, args, note, auto?, credits? }: call it as given. Returns { verdict: complete | playable_with_defects | incomplete, headline, genre, counts, defects, next (ordered calls), sections, text, play_url }. fix=true first applies what is free and safe (the best free Library model on each capsule — rebind at will —, the free standard clips, the suggested control scheme) and reports it in fixes. playtest="run" plays the game headless first (5–20 s); the default reads the last playtest and says when it is stale. Never refuses a write and never spends: paid fixes (a priced model, a rig, a generation) come back with their price to ask the user about. Aim for verdict complete; if you stop before, tell the user exactly what is left. 0 credits.

brief.description: Free words about the game (theme, setting): they weigh in the model proposals.

fix.description: true: apply the free and safe fixes first (free models on capsules, standard clips, suggested control scheme), then read. Nothing paid is ever done.

playtest.description: last (default): read the stored playtest of the project. run: play it headless now, then read.

project_id.description: Game Kit project id (gkp_…). Not a dedicated-server project (gpj_…) nor a Library item.

workspace_id.description: Workspace authorized by the current key. Never infer another user’s workspace.
